newsitem.title: DUBAI: Denmark's apology to Rushdie insult to Islam - Iran.
newsitem.headline: Denmark's apology to Rushdie insult to Islam - Iran.

text.p: Iran has termed Denmark's apology for postponing a planned visit by British writer Salman Rushdie as an insult to the world's Moslems, the official Iranian news agency IRNA reported.
It quoted Foreign Ministry spokesman Mohamad Mohammadi as saying on Tuesday that Denmark's apology had "increased the disgust of Moslems whose religious beliefs had been insulted."

Mohammadi said awarding Rushdie -- who faces a death threat from Iran over his novel "The Satanic Verses" -- a European literary award was "tantamount to seconding Rushdie's insult to the world's Moslems."
He said Rushdie had become "an evil political tool."
Denmark last week bowed to international pressure and invited Rushdie to fly to Copenhagen to receive the award. It apologised for originally barring him citing security reasons.

Indian-born Rushdie has lived in hiding and with permanent protection since 1989 when Iran's late spiritual leader Ayatollah Ruhollah Khomeini issued a fatwa against him for blaspheming Islamic in his book.

Tehran says it would not send anyone to kill the author. But European officials say this would probably be insufficient to solve the long-running crisis without a further commitment to prevent others from doing so.
